newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: FORECAST-Kazakh 1997 inflation seen at 17.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Kazakh 1997 inflation seen at 17.5 pct.

text.p: Inflation for 1997 in Kazakhstan will be no higher than 17.5 percent, Kazakh economy minister Omirzak Shukeyev told the central Asian nation's parliament on Thursday.
"In the budget prepared for next year, we calculated inflation at no higher than 17.5 percent," the minister said.
He said inflation for the first nine months of this year averaged 21.2 percent.
"In 1996 there has been a sharp rise in prices for utilities but next year this factor will not make a marked impact on the inflation process," Shukeyev said.
The minister also told deputies that the government estimated next year's budget deficit at three percent of gross domestic product.
